--- aliases: - geolocator-intro.html --- # Publish your data This tutorial explains how to create a GeoLocator Data Package (GeoLocator DP) from a GeoPressureTemplate project, upload it to Zenodo, and validate the draft before publication. ::: callout-note For an introduction to this format, visit the [GeoLocator DP website](https://geopressure.org/GeoLocator-DP/). ::: ## Install GeoLocatoR We use the [GeoLocatoR](https://geopressure.org/GeoLocatoR) package to create and validate the data package. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # install.packages("pak") pak::pkg_install("GeoPressure/GeoLocatoR") ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(GeoLocatoR) ``` ::: ## Step 1. Create the package from GeoPressureTemplate Read your project and build a geolocator-dp object. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pkg <- read_geopressuretemplate() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning: ! Dropped 1 column from "edges" not defined by its schema: name. i "edges" declares `fieldsMatch: superset`, which allows only the columns its schema defines. ``` ::: ::: By default, `read_geopressuretemplate()` reads `data/interim/*.RData` first and falls back to raw data for tags without interim files. - Use `from` to force a specific source (`"interim"` or `"raw-tag"`). - Prefix a file/folder with `_` to exclude a tag temporarily. Inspect the package summary: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} print(pkg) ## ## -- A GeoLocator Data Package `pkg` (v1.2) -------------------------------------- ## ## -- Metadata ## Note: All green texts are fields of `pkg` which can be accessed with ## `pkg$field`. ## * temporal: "2017-06-20" to "2022-06-11" ## * taxonomic: "Acrocephalus arundinaceus" and "Limnothlypis swainsonii" ## * numberTags: tags: 2, measurements: 2, light: 1, pressure: 2, activity: 1, ## temperature_external: 2, paths: 2 ## ## -- Resources: (7 resources) ## * `tags()` (n=2) ## * `observations()` (n=4) ## * `measurements()` (n=336,562) ## * `staps()` (n=38) ## * `twilights()` (n=632) ## * `paths()` (n=418) ## * `edges()` (n=308) ``` ::: ## Step 2. Complete `tags` and `observations` At this point, `tags` and `observations` will certaintly still be missing key metadata (for example ringing information). The easiest way to fix this is to export the tables, edit them manually and then save them back. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} write.csv(tags(pkg), file = "data/tags.csv", row.names = FALSE) write.csv(observations(pkg), file = "data/observations.csv", row.names = FALSE) ``` ::: Rebuild and validate after editing: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pkg <- read_geopressuretemplate() ## \ Reading 1/2 interim tags. ## v Read 2 interim tags. ## ## Warning: ! Dropped 1 column from "edges" not defined by its schema: name. ## i "edges" declares `fieldsMatch: superset`, which allows only the columns its ## schema defines. ## v Reading tags from './data/tags.csv'. ## v Reading observations from './data/observations.csv'. validate_gldp(pkg) ## ## -- Check Profile ## ## -- Check Resources tags ## v Table tags is consistent with the schema. ## ## -- Check Resources observations ## v Table observations is consistent with the schema. ## ## -- Check Resources measurements ## v Table measurements is consistent with the schema. ## ## -- Check Resources staps ## v Table staps is consistent with the schema. ## ## -- Check Resources twilights ## v Table twilights is consistent with the schema. ## ## -- Check Resources paths ## v Table paths is consistent with the schema. ## ## -- Check Resources edges ## v Table edges is consistent with the schema. ## ## -- Check Coherence ## v Coherence checks passed. ## ## -- Check Metadata ## ! pkg$title is missing or empty. ## ! Missing roles in pkg$contributors. ## ! Expected pkg$record_type to be "dataset"; got NA. ## ! No relatedIdentifiers present. Add any resources related to the data (e.g. papers, project pages, derived datasets, etc.). ## ! Missing selected community . ## ! Missing or invalid pkg$codeRepository; expected a GitHub repository URL. ## ## -- Final: ---------------------------------------------------------------------- ## v Package validation succeeded. ``` ::: ## Step 3. Run visual checks In this final stage, we check the coverage, tag count, and deployment/retrieval consistency to avoid outliers or missing information. To do so, plot each variable and check that (1) all the ring numbers are present, (2) all measurements are correct and no information is missing and (3) trajectories are correct. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(pkg, "ring") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](geolocator-create_files/figure-html/15-plot-pkg-coverage-1.png){width=672} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} plot(pkg, "coverage") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range (`geom_tile()`). ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](geolocator-create_files/figure-html/15-plot-pkg-coverage-2.png){width=672} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} plot(pkg, "map") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Step 4. Write the package files Now that we have checked the data, we can export `pkg` into the `csv` file that will be uploaded on Zenodo. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} write_gldp(pkg, "data/datapackage") ``` ::: ## Step 5. Create the Zenodo draft record [Create a new draft on Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/uploads/new), complete all metadata fields, BUT, do not submit it just yet. ::: callout-warning ## Mandatory checklist Complete **all** items below. If one or more are missing, the record may be returned for revision and not accepted in the community. - [ ] Select the community: GeoLocator Data Package - [ ] Upload all files - [ ] Reserve a DOI - [ ] Set resource type to Dataset - [ ] Add a title starting with "GeoLocator Data Package:" - [ ] Add all data package authors (with roles when possible) - [ ] Add a basic description - [ ] Add funding and related resources - [ ] Add the GitHub link of the GeoPressureTemplate used - [ ] Add any additional metadata you want to include Review the [GeoLocator DP curation policy](https://geopressure.org/GeoLocator-DP/curation) before submission. ::: ## Step 6. Validate the Zenodo draft Before submitting, read the draft back and validate exactly what Zenodo contains. ::: callout-info Reading a draft requires a Zenodo API token. Create one at [Zenodo token settings](https://zenodo.org/account/settings/applications/tokens/new/) and save it in your keyring: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} keyring::key_set_with_value("ZENODO_TOKEN", password = "{your_zenodo_token}") ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pkg <- read_zenodo( "10.5072/zenodo.472302", draft = TRUE, # Draft record sandbox = TRUE # Remove if using production Zenodo ) ``` ::: ::: callout-important Run the official validation check on the draft package: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} validate_gldp(pkg) ``` ::: If validation reports errors, fix the metadata/files and run the check again until valid. ::: ## Step 7. Submit Once all checks are valid and metadata are complete, submit the Zenodo record! 🎉 A curator will review the data and get back to you if any revision is required.
